LECTURE 16 Stage 3: Attention

Multi-Head Attention

Letting the model attend to multiple relationships simultaneously
⏱ 50 min read 💻 Hands-on coding 🎯 Advanced

Why Multiple Heads?

In the previous lecture, we built a single attention mechanism that computes one set of attention weights. But think about how you read a sentence like "The cat sat on the mat because it was tired." When you process "it," you simultaneously track multiple relationships: "it" refers to "cat" (coreference), "it" is the subject of "was tired" (syntactic role), and the whole clause modifies the earlier event (discourse structure). A single attention head can only compute one weighted combination of values — it collapses all these relationships into a single pattern.

Multi-head attention solves this by running several attention computations in parallel, each with its own learned projections. Each "head" can specialize in different types of relationships:

  • Head 1 might learn to attend to the previous word (local syntax)
  • Head 2 might track subject-verb agreement across long distances
  • Head 3 might capture coreference ("it" → "cat")
  • Head 4 might attend to punctuation and sentence boundaries
Key Insight: Multi-head attention is like having a committee of experts, each examining the input from a different perspective. The final output combines all their findings. This is one of the most important architectural innovations in the Transformer.

The Mechanics: Splitting Q, K, V Across Heads

The key idea is surprisingly simple. Instead of having one large set of Q, K, V projections with dimension d_model, we split the model dimension into h heads, each operating on a dimension of d_k = d_model / h.

For a model with d_model = 512 and h = 8 heads:

  • Each head works with d_k = 512 / 8 = 64 dimensions
  • Each head has its own W_Q, W_K, W_V matrices of size (512, 64)
  • All heads compute attention in parallel
  • Outputs are concatenated back to 512 dimensions
  • A final projection W_O maps the concatenated result

Crucially, the total computation is roughly the same as single-head attention with the full dimension. We are not adding computation — we are dividing it across specialized subspaces.

Pro Tip: In practice, rather than creating separate weight matrices per head, we use a single large projection and then reshape the result into multiple heads. This is more efficient for GPU computation. We will implement both approaches so you understand the equivalence.

Step-by-Step: How Multi-Head Attention Works

Step 1: Project inputs into Q, K, V

Given input X of shape (batch, seq_len, d_model), compute:

  • Q = X @ W_Q — shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • K = X @ W_K — shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • V = X @ W_V — shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)

Step 2: Reshape into multiple heads

Reshape Q, K, V from (batch, seq_len, d_model) to (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). This is the critical step — we split the last dimension and transpose so each head has its own attention subspace.

Step 3: Compute attention per head

Each head independently computes scaled dot-product attention on its own d_k-dimensional subspace.

Step 4: Concatenate heads

Reshape the output from (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) back to (batch, seq_len, d_model).

Step 5: Output projection

Apply a final linear projection W_O to combine information from all heads.

Code: Multi-Head Splitting and Reshaping

Let us start by understanding the reshape operation that is at the heart of multi-head attention. This is often the most confusing part, so we will visualize it carefully.

Python

import numpy as np

def split_heads(x, n_heads):
    """Split the last dimension into (n_heads, d_k).

    Input shape:  (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    Output shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    """
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)

    # Transpose: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    return x

def merge_heads(x):
    """Reverse of split_heads.

    Input shape:  (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    Output shape: (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    """
    batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k = x.shape

    # Transpose back: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads * d_k)

    return x

# Demonstrate with concrete shapes
batch_size = 2
seq_len = 4
d_model = 8
n_heads = 2
d_k = d_model // n_heads  # 4

np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)

print(f"Input shape: {x.shape}")
print(f"d_model={d_model}, n_heads={n_heads}, d_k={d_k}")
print()

# Split into heads
x_split = split_heads(x, n_heads)
print(f"After split_heads: {x_split.shape}")
print(f"  Head 0, token 0: {x_split[0, 0, 0, :]}")
print(f"  Head 1, token 0: {x_split[0, 1, 0, :]}")
print()

# Verify: original first token had 8 dims, now split into 2 heads of 4
print(f"Original token 0, batch 0: {x[0, 0, :]}")
print(f"Head 0 gets first {d_k} dims:  {x[0, 0, :d_k]}")
print(f"Head 1 gets last {d_k} dims:   {x[0, 0, d_k:]}")
print()

# Merge back
x_merged = merge_heads(x_split)
print(f"After merge_heads: {x_merged.shape}")
print(f"Reconstruction matches original: {np.allclose(x, x_merged)}")

Parallel Attention Computation

Once we have split Q, K, V into heads, each head computes its own attention independently. The beauty of this design is that with proper reshaping, we can compute all heads in a single batched matrix multiplication — no loops required.

Think of it this way: after splitting, we have a tensor of shape (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). NumPy (and PyTorch) treats the first two dimensions as "batch" dimensions, so a single matrix multiply computes attention for all batch elements and all heads simultaneously.

Key Insight: The "parallel" in multi-head attention is not just conceptual — it is literal. On a GPU, all heads compute simultaneously with no sequential dependency. This is why multi-head attention with 8 heads of d_k=64 is roughly as fast as single-head attention with d=512.

Code: Complete MultiHeadAttention Class

Now let us build the complete multi-head attention module. This implementation follows the same structure used in GPT-2, BERT, and most modern Transformers.

Python

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    """Numerically stable softmax."""
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    """Multi-Head Attention mechanism from 'Attention Is All You Need'.

    This implementation closely follows the original Transformer paper
    and is structured similarly to how PyTorch implements it.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0, "d_model must be divisible by n_heads"

        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)  # Xavier-like init

        # Combined projections (more efficient than per-head)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

        # Biases
        self.b_q = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_k = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_v = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_o = np.zeros(d_model)

    def split_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)"""
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k)
        return x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    def merge_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)"""
        batch, _, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        return x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)

    def forward(self, x, mask=None, return_attention=False):
        """Forward pass of multi-head attention.

        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            mask: Optional causal mask
            return_attention: If True, also return attention weights per head

        Returns:
            output: Shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            attn_weights: Shape (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len) if requested
        """
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

        # Step 1: Linear projections
        Q = x @ self.W_q + self.b_q  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        K = x @ self.W_k + self.b_k
        V = x @ self.W_v + self.b_v

        # Step 2: Split into heads
        Q = self.split_heads(Q)  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
        K = self.split_heads(K)
        V = self.split_heads(V)

        # Step 3: Scaled dot-product attention (all heads in parallel)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        # scores shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)

        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)

        attn_weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1)

        # Step 4: Apply attention to values
        context = attn_weights @ V  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)

        # Step 5: Merge heads and apply output projection
        context = self.merge_heads(context)  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        output = context @ self.W_o + self.b_o

        if return_attention:
            return output, attn_weights
        return output

# Test it
np.random.seed(42)
d_model = 16
n_heads = 4
seq_len = 6
batch_size = 1

mha = MultiHeadAttention(d_model=d_model, n_heads=n_heads, seed=0)
x = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)

# Create causal mask (for autoregressive / GPT-style models)
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)

output, attn = mha.forward(x, mask=causal_mask, return_attention=True)

print(f"Input shape:  {x.shape}")
print(f"Output shape: {output.shape}")
print(f"Attention weights shape: {attn.shape}")
print(f"  (batch={batch_size}, heads={n_heads}, seq={seq_len}, seq={seq_len})")
print()
print(f"d_k per head: {mha.d_k}")
print(f"Total parameters: {sum(w.size for w in [mha.W_q, mha.W_k, mha.W_v, mha.W_o])}")
print()

# Verify causal masking: each position only attends to itself and earlier
print("Attention weights for Head 0 (notice the causal pattern):")
print("Each row sums to 1, and upper triangle is ~0:")
print(np.round(attn[0, 0], 3))

Comparing Single-Head vs Multi-Head Attention

To understand why multiple heads help, let us compare the attention patterns. With a single head, the model must compress all relationship types into one attention distribution. With multiple heads, each head can capture a different pattern.

Consider the sentence: "The cat sat on the mat." A single head attending from "sat" must choose: attend to "cat" (the subject) or to "on" (the next word for syntax) or spread attention thinly. Multiple heads can do all of these simultaneously.

Important: The advantage of multi-head attention is not that it has more parameters. If you compare single-head attention with d_model=512 to 8-head attention with d_k=64, the parameter count is the same. The advantage is purely structural: the model can maintain multiple distinct attention patterns.

Code: Comparing Attention Patterns Across Heads

Python

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = attn @ V
        context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
        return context @ self.W_o, attn

# Simulate token embeddings for "The cat sat on the mat"
tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
d_model = 32
n_heads = 4
np.random.seed(123)
x = np.random.randn(1, len(tokens), d_model)

causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((len(tokens), len(tokens))), k=1)
mha = MultiHeadAttention(d_model=d_model, n_heads=n_heads, seed=7)
output, attn_weights = mha.forward(x, mask=causal_mask)

# Analyze each head's attention pattern
print("=== Attention Pattern Analysis ===")
print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")
print()

for head_idx in range(n_heads):
    head_attn = attn_weights[0, head_idx]
    print(f"--- Head {head_idx} ---")

    # What does each token primarily attend to?
    for tok_idx, tok in enumerate(tokens):
        top_k = min(3, tok_idx + 1)
        attn_row = head_attn[tok_idx, :tok_idx+1]
        top_indices = np.argsort(attn_row)[-top_k:][::-1]
        top_tokens = [(tokens[i], f"{attn_row[i]:.3f}") for i in top_indices]
        print(f"  '{tok}' attends to: {top_tokens}")
    print()

# Quantify head diversity
print("=== Head Diversity Analysis ===")
# Compare attention distributions between heads
for i in range(n_heads):
    for j in range(i+1, n_heads):
        # Average absolute difference in attention patterns
        diff = np.mean(np.abs(attn_weights[0, i] - attn_weights[0, j]))
        print(f"  Avg difference between Head {i} and Head {j}: {diff:.4f}")

print()
# How "focused" is each head? (lower entropy = more focused)
for head_idx in range(n_heads):
    head_attn = attn_weights[0, head_idx]
    # Compute average entropy across tokens
    entropies = []
    for tok_idx in range(len(tokens)):
        row = head_attn[tok_idx, :tok_idx+1]
        row = row[row > 1e-10]
        entropy = -np.sum(row * np.log(row))
        entropies.append(entropy)
    avg_entropy = np.mean(entropies)
    print(f"  Head {head_idx} average entropy: {avg_entropy:.4f} "
          f"({'focused' if avg_entropy < 0.8 else 'distributed'})")

How Many Heads? Design Tradeoffs

The number of attention heads is a key hyperparameter. Here are the tradeoffs:

Model d_model Heads d_k
GPT-2 Small 768 12 64
GPT-3 12288 96 128
Llama 2 7B 4096 32 128
Llama 3 70B 8192 64 128

More heads (smaller d_k): More diverse attention patterns, but each head has a smaller subspace to work with. Below d_k=32, individual heads may lack representational capacity.

Fewer heads (larger d_k): Each head has richer representations but fewer distinct patterns. Single-head attention is the extreme case.

The sweet spot: Most modern models use d_k=64 or d_k=128. The original Transformer paper used d_k=64 with 8 heads, and this has proven robust across many architectures.

Pro Tip: Research has shown that not all heads are equally important. Some heads can be pruned after training with minimal performance loss. This is the basis for structured pruning techniques used to make models faster at inference time.

Code: Measuring the Effect of Head Count

Python

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

def multi_head_attention(x, n_heads, W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, mask=None):
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    Q = (x @ W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    K = (x @ W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    V = (x @ W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

    scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
    attn = softmax(scores)

    context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, d_model)
    return context @ W_o, attn

# Compare different head counts with the same d_model
d_model = 64
seq_len = 8
batch_size = 1
np.random.seed(42)
x = np.random.randn(batch_size, seq_len, d_model)
causal_mask = np.triu(np.ones((seq_len, seq_len)), k=1)

print(f"d_model = {d_model}, seq_len = {seq_len}")
print(f"{'='*55}")

for n_heads in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]:
    d_k = d_model // n_heads
    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
    scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
    W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
    W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
    W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
    W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

    output, attn = multi_head_attention(x, n_heads, W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, causal_mask)

    # Measure diversity: average pairwise difference between heads
    if n_heads > 1:
        diffs = []
        for i in range(n_heads):
            for j in range(i+1, n_heads):
                diffs.append(np.mean(np.abs(attn[0,i] - attn[0,j])))
        avg_diversity = np.mean(diffs)
    else:
        avg_diversity = 0.0

    # Measure entropy of each head
    head_entropies = []
    for h in range(n_heads):
        for t in range(seq_len):
            row = attn[0, h, t, :t+1]
            row = row[row > 1e-10]
            head_entropies.append(-np.sum(row * np.log(row)))
    avg_entropy = np.mean(head_entropies)

    print(f"  {n_heads:2d} heads (d_k={d_k:2d}): "
          f"diversity={avg_diversity:.4f}, "
          f"avg_entropy={avg_entropy:.3f}, "
          f"output_norm={np.linalg.norm(output):.2f}")

Key Takeaways

  • Multi-head attention runs several attention computations in parallel, each with its own learned projections operating on a subspace of dimension d_k = d_model / n_heads.
  • The total parameter count is the same as single-head attention — we trade one large attention space for multiple smaller specialized ones.
  • The critical operations are split_heads (reshape + transpose) and merge_heads (transpose + reshape), which partition and reassemble the model dimension.
  • Different heads learn to capture different types of relationships (syntactic, semantic, positional), making the model more expressive than any single attention pattern.
  • Modern LLMs typically use d_k=64 or d_k=128 per head, with the total number of heads determined by d_model / d_k.

LECȚIA 16 Etapa 3: Atenție

Atenție Multi-Head

Permițând modelului să participe la mai multe relații simultan
⏱ 50 min lectură 💻 Programare practică 🎯 Avansat

De ce mai multe capete?

În lecția anterioară, am construit un singur mecanism de atenție care calculează un set de ponderi de atenție. Dar gândiți-vă cum citiți o propoziție precum „Pisica a stat pe covor pentru că era obosită." Când procesați „era", urmăriți simultan mai multe relații: „era" se referă la „pisica" (coreferență), „era" este subiectul lui „obosită" (rol sintactic), iar întreaga propoziție subordonată modifică evenimentul anterior (structură discursivă). Un singur cap de atenție poate calcula doar o singură combinație ponderată de valori — comprimând toate aceste relații într-un singur tipar.

Atenția multi-head rezolvă acest lucru prin rularea mai multor calcule de atenție în paralel, fiecare cu propriile proiecții învățate. Fiecare „cap" se poate specializa pe tipuri diferite de relații:

  • Capul 1 ar putea învăța să acorde atenție cuvântului anterior (sintaxă locală)
  • Capul 2 ar putea urmări acordul subiect-verb pe distanțe lungi
  • Capul 3 ar putea capta coreferința („era" → „pisica")
  • Capul 4 ar putea acorda atenție punctuației și limitelor de propoziție
Observație cheie: Atenția multi-head este ca un comitet de experți, fiecare examinând intrarea dintr-o perspectivă diferită. Rezultatul final combină toate descoperirile lor. Aceasta este una dintre cele mai importante inovații arhitecturale din Transformer.

Mecanica: Împărțirea Q, K, V între capete

Ideea cheie este surprinzător de simplă. În loc să avem un singur set mare de proiecții Q, K, V cu dimensiunea d_model, împărțim dimensiunea modelului în h capete, fiecare operând pe o dimensiune de d_k = d_model / h.

Pentru un model cu d_model = 512 și h = 8 capete:

  • Fiecare cap lucrează cu d_k = 512 / 8 = 64 dimensiuni
  • Fiecare cap are propriile matrice W_Q, W_K, W_V de dimensiune (512, 64)
  • Toate capetele calculează atenția în paralel
  • Ieșirile sunt concatenate înapoi la 512 dimensiuni
  • O proiecție finală W_O mapează rezultatul concatenat

Este esențial de menționat că volumul total de calcul este aproximativ același ca la atenția cu un singur cap cu dimensiunea completă. Nu adăugăm calcule — le împărțim între subspații specializate.

Sfat profesional: În practică, în loc să creăm matrice de ponderi separate per cap, folosim o singură proiecție mare și apoi remodelăm rezultatul în mai multe capete. Aceasta este mai eficientă pentru calculul pe GPU. Vom implementa ambele abordări pentru a înțelege echivalența.

Pas cu pas: Cum funcționează atenția Multi-Head

Pasul 1: Proiectarea intrărilor în Q, K, V

Dat fiind inputul X de formă (batch, seq_len, d_model), calculăm:

  • Q = X @ W_Q — forma (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • K = X @ W_K — forma (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • V = X @ W_V — forma (batch, seq_len, d_model)

Pasul 2: Remodelarea în mai multe capete

Remodelăm Q, K, V din (batch, seq_len, d_model) în (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). Acesta este pasul critic — împărțim ultima dimensiune și transpunem astfel încât fiecare cap să aibă propriul subspațiu de atenție.

Pasul 3: Calcularea atenției per cap

Fiecare cap calculează independent atenția scaled dot-product pe propriul subspațiu de d_k dimensiuni.

Pasul 4: Concatenarea capetelor

Remodelăm ieșirea din (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) înapoi la (batch, seq_len, d_model).

Pasul 5: Proiecția de ieșire

Aplicăm o proiecție liniară finală W_O pentru a combina informațiile de la toate capetele.

Cod: Împărțirea și remodelarea Multi-Head

Să începem prin a înțelege operația de remodelare care este în centrul atenției multi-head. Aceasta este adesea partea cea mai confuză, așa că o vom vizualiza cu atenție.

import numpy as np

def split_heads(x, n_heads):
    """Split the last dimension into (n_heads, d_k).

    Input shape:  (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    Output shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    """
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)

    # Transpose: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    return x

def merge_heads(x):
    """Reverse of split_heads.

    Input shape:  (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    Output shape: (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    """
    batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k = x.shape

    # Transpose back: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads * d_k)

    return x

Calculul paralel al atenției

Odată ce am împărțit Q, K, V în capete, fiecare cap își calculează propria atenție independent. Frumusețea acestui design este că, cu o remodelare adecvată, putem calcula toate capetele într-o singură înmulțire matriceală pe loturi — fără bucle necesare.

Gândiți-vă în felul următor: după împărțire, avem un tensor de formă (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). NumPy (și PyTorch) tratează primele două dimensiuni ca dimensiuni de „lot", astfel încât o singură înmulțire matriceală calculează atenția pentru toate elementele din lot și toate capetele simultan.

Observație cheie: „Paralelul" din atenția multi-head nu este doar conceptual — este literal. Pe un GPU, toate capetele calculează simultan fără nicio dependență secvențială. De aceea atenția multi-head cu 8 capete de d_k=64 este aproximativ la fel de rapidă ca atenția cu un singur cap cu d=512.

Cod: Clasa completă MultiHeadAttention

Acum să construim modulul complet de atenție multi-head. Această implementare urmează aceeași structură folosită în GPT-2, BERT și cele mai multe Transformere moderne.

Python

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    """Numerically stable softmax."""
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    """Multi-Head Attention mechanism from 'Attention Is All You Need'.

    This implementation closely follows the original Transformer paper
    and is structured similarly to how PyTorch implements it.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0, "d_model must be divisible by n_heads"

        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)  # Xavier-like init

        # Combined projections (more efficient than per-head)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

        # Biases
        self.b_q = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_k = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_v = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_o = np.zeros(d_model)

    def split_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)"""
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k)
        return x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    def merge_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)"""
        batch, _, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        return x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)

    def forward(self, x, mask=None, return_attention=False):
        """Forward pass of multi-head attention.

        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            mask: Optional causal mask
            return_attention: If True, also return attention weights per head

        Returns:
            output: Shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            attn_weights: Shape (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len) if requested
        """
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

        # Step 1: Linear projections
        Q = x @ self.W_q + self.b_q  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        K = x @ self.W_k + self.b_k
        V = x @ self.W_v + self.b_v

        # Step 2: Split into heads
        Q = self.split_heads(Q)  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
        K = self.split_heads(K)
        V = self.split_heads(V)

        # Step 3: Scaled dot-product attention (all heads in parallel)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        # scores shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)

        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)

        attn_weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1)

        # Step 4: Apply attention to values
        context = attn_weights @ V  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)

        # Step 5: Merge heads and apply output projection
        context = self.merge_heads(context)  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        output = context @ self.W_o + self.b_o

        if return_attention:
            return output, attn_weights
        return output

Comparația dintre atenția cu un singur cap și atenția Multi-Head

Pentru a înțelege de ce mai multe capete ajută, să comparăm tiparele de atenție. Cu un singur cap, modelul trebuie să comprima toate tipurile de relații într-o singură distribuție de atenție. Cu mai multe capete, fiecare cap poate capta un tipar diferit.

Luați în considerare propoziția: „Pisica a stat pe covor." Un singur cap care acordă atenție de la „a stat" trebuie să aleagă: să acorde atenție la „pisica" (subiectul) sau la „pe" (următorul cuvânt pentru sintaxă) sau să distribuie atenția subțire. Mai multe capete pot face toate acestea simultan.

Important: Avantajul atenției multi-head nu este că are mai mulți parametri. Dacă comparați atenția cu un singur cap cu d_model=512 cu atenția cu 8 capete cu d_k=64, numărul de parametri este același. Avantajul este pur structural: modelul poate menține mai multe tipare de atenție distincte.

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = attn @ V
        context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
        return context @ self.W_o, attn

Numărul de capete de atenție este un hiperparametru cheie. Iată compromisurile:

Model d_model Capete d_k
GPT-2 Small 768 12 64
GPT-3 12288 96 128
Llama 2 7B 4096 32 128
Llama 3 70B 8192 64 128

Mai multe capete (d_k mai mic): Tipare de atenție mai diverse, dar fiecare cap are un subspațiu mai mic cu care să lucreze. Sub d_k=32, capetele individuale pot avea capacitate reprezentațională insuficientă.

Mai puține capete (d_k mai mare): Fiecare cap are reprezentări mai bogate, dar mai puține tipare distincte. Atenția cu un singur cap este cazul extrem.

Punctul optim: Cele mai multe modele moderne folosesc d_k=64 sau d_k=128. Lucrarea originală Transformer a folosit d_k=64 cu 8 capete, și aceasta s-a dovedit robustă în multe arhitecturi.

Sfat profesional: Cercetările au arătat că nu toate capetele sunt la fel de importante. Unele capete pot fi eliminate după antrenament cu pierderi minime de performanță. Aceasta este baza tehnicilor de tăiere structurată folosite pentru a face modelele mai rapide la inferență.

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

def multi_head_attention(x, n_heads, W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, mask=None):
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    Q = (x @ W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    K = (x @ W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    V = (x @ W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

    scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
    attn = softmax(scores)

    context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, d_model)
    return context @ W_o, attn

  • Atenția multi-head rulează mai multe calcule de atenție în paralel, fiecare cu propriile proiecții învățate, operând pe un subspațiu de dimensiune d_k = d_model / n_heads.
  • Numărul total de parametri este același ca la atenția cu un singur cap — schimbăm un spațiu de atenție mare cu mai multe spații specializate mai mici.
  • Operațiile critice sunt split_heads (remodelare + transpunere) și merge_heads (transpunere + remodelare), care partiționează și reasamblează dimensiunea modelului.
  • Diferite capete învață să capteze tipuri diferite de relații (sintactice, semantice, poziționale), făcând modelul mai expresiv decât orice tipar de atenție individual.
  • LLM-urile moderne folosesc de obicei d_k=64 sau d_k=128 per cap, cu numărul total de capete determinat de d_model / d_k.

Γιατι Πολλαπλες Κεφαλες;

Στην προηγουμενη διαλεξη, κατασκευασαμε εναν μεμονωμενο μηχανισμο προσοχης που υπολογιζει ενα σετ βαρων προσοχης. Μια μοναδικη κεφαλη προσοχης μπορει να υπολογισει μονο εναν σταθμισμενο συνδυασμο τιμων — συμπτυσσει ολες αυτες τις σχεσεις σε ενα μοναδικο μοτιβο.

Η πολυκεφαλη προσοχη λυνει αυτο το προβλημα εκτελωντας πολλους υπολογισμους προσοχης παραλληλα, καθεναν με τις δικες του μαθημενες προβολες. Καθε «κεφαλη» μπορει να εξειδικευτει σε διαφορετικους τυπους σχεσεων:

  • Κεφαλη 1 μπορει να μαθει να εστιαζει στην προηγουμενη λεξη (τοπικο συντακτικο)
  • Κεφαλη 2 μπορει να παρακολουθει τη συμφωνια υποκειμενου-ρηματος σε μεγαλες αποστασεις
  • Κεφαλη 3 μπορει να συλλαμβανει τη συναναφορα («it» → «cat»)
  • Κεφαλη 4 μπορει να εστιαζει στα σημεια στιξης και στα ορια προτασεων
Βασικη Ιδεα: Η πολυκεφαλη προσοχη ειναι σαν να εχετε μια επιτροπη ειδικων, καθενας απο τους οποιους εξεταζει την εισοδο απο διαφορετικη οπτικη γωνια. Η τελικη εξοδος συνδυαζει ολα τα ευρηματα τους. Αυτη ειναι μια απο τις πιο σημαντικες αρχιτεκτονικες καινοτομιες στο Transformer.

Ο Μηχανισμος: Διαχωρισμος Q, K, V σε Κεφαλες

Η βασικη ιδεα ειναι εκπληκτικα απλη. Αντι να εχουμε ενα μεγαλο σετ προβολων Q, K, V με διασταση d_model, διαχωριζουμε τη διασταση του μοντελου σε h κεφαλες, καθεμια λειτουργωντας σε διασταση d_k = d_model / h.

Για ενα μοντελο με d_model = 512 και h = 8 κεφαλες:

  • Καθε κεφαλη εργαζεται με d_k = 512 / 8 = 64 διαστασεις
  • Καθε κεφαλη εχει τους δικους της πινακες W_Q, W_K, W_V μεγεθους (512, 64)
  • Ολες οι κεφαλες υπολογιζουν την προσοχη παραλληλα
  • Οι εξοδοι συνενωνονται πισω σε 512 διαστασεις
  • Μια τελικη προβολη W_O απεικονιζει το συνενωμενο αποτελεσμα

Κρισιμα, ο συνολικος υπολογισμος ειναι περιπου ο ιδιος με την προσοχη μοναδικης κεφαλης με πληρη διασταση. Δεν προσθετουμε υπολογισμο — τον διαιρουμε σε εξειδικευμενους υποχωρους.

Συμβουλη: Στην πραξη, αντι να δημιουργουμε ξεχωριστους πινακες βαρων ανα κεφαλη, χρησιμοποιουμε μια μοναδικη μεγαλη προβολη και στη συνεχεια αναδιαμορφωνουμε το αποτελεσμα σε πολλαπλες κεφαλες. Αυτο ειναι πιο αποδοτικο για υπολογισμο σε GPU. Θα υλοποιησουμε και τις δυο προσεγγισεις ωστε να κατανοησετε την ισοδυναμια.

Βημα προς Βημα: Πως Λειτουργει η Πολυκεφαλη Προσοχη

Βημα 1: Προβολη εισοδων σε Q, K, V

Δεδομενης εισοδου X σχηματος (batch, seq_len, d_model), υπολογιζουμε:

  • Q = X @ W_Q — σχημα (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • K = X @ W_K — σχημα (batch, seq_len, d_model)
  • V = X @ W_V — σχημα (batch, seq_len, d_model)

Βημα 2: Αναδιαμορφωση σε πολλαπλες κεφαλες

Αναδιαμορφωνουμε τα Q, K, V απο (batch, seq_len, d_model) σε (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). Αυτο ειναι το κρισιμο βημα — διαχωριζουμε την τελευταια διασταση και μεταθετουμε ωστε καθε κεφαλη να εχει τον δικο της υποχωρο προσοχης.

Βημα 3: Υπολογισμος προσοχης ανα κεφαλη

Καθε κεφαλη υπολογιζει ανεξαρτητα κλιμακουμενο εσωτερικο γινομενο προσοχης στον δικο της υποχωρο d_k διαστασεων.

Βημα 4: Συνενωση κεφαλων

Αναδιαμορφωνουμε την εξοδο απο (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) πισω σε (batch, seq_len, d_model).

Βημα 5: Προβολη εξοδου

Εφαρμοζουμε μια τελικη γραμμικη προβολη W_O για να συνδυασουμε τις πληροφοριες απο ολες τις κεφαλες.

import numpy as np

def split_heads(x, n_heads):
    """Split the last dimension into (n_heads, d_k).

    Input shape:  (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    Output shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    """
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)

    # Transpose: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    return x

def merge_heads(x):
    """Reverse of split_heads.

    Input shape:  (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
    Output shape: (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    """
    batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k = x.shape

    # Transpose back: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k)
    x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    # Reshape: (batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)
    x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads * d_k)

    return x

Παραλληλος Υπολογισμος Προσοχης

Μολις διαχωρισουμε τα Q, K, V σε κεφαλες, καθε κεφαλη υπολογιζει τη δικη της προσοχη ανεξαρτητα. Η ομορφια αυτου του σχεδιασμου ειναι οτι με σωστη αναδιαμορφωση, μπορουμε να υπολογισουμε ολες τις κεφαλες με εναν μοναδικο ομαδικο πολλαπλασιασμο πινακων — χωρις βροχους.

Σκεφτειτε το ως εξης: μετα τον διαχωρισμο, εχουμε εναν τανυστη σχηματος (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k). Το NumPy (και το PyTorch) αντιμετωπιζει τις πρωτες δυο διαστασεις ως διαστασεις «παρτιδας», οποτε ενας μοναδικος πολλαπλασιασμος πινακων υπολογιζει την προσοχη για ολα τα στοιχεια της παρτιδας και ολες τις κεφαλες ταυτοχρονα.

Βασικη Ιδεα: Ο «παραλληλισμος» στην πολυκεφαλη προσοχη δεν ειναι μονο εννοιολογικος — ειναι κυριολεκτικος. Σε μια GPU, ολες οι κεφαλες υπολογιζονται ταυτοχρονα χωρις διαδοχικη εξαρτηση. Γιαυτο η πολυκεφαλη προσοχη με 8 κεφαλες d_k=64 ειναι περιπου το ιδιο γρηγορη με την προσοχη μοναδικης κεφαλης με d=512.

import numpy as np

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
    """Numerically stable softmax."""
    x_max = np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)
    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    """Multi-Head Attention mechanism from 'Attention Is All You Need'.

    This implementation closely follows the original Transformer paper
    and is structured similarly to how PyTorch implements it.
    """

    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0, "d_model must be divisible by n_heads"

        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads

        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)  # Xavier-like init

        # Combined projections (more efficient than per-head)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

        # Biases
        self.b_q = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_k = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_v = np.zeros(d_model)
        self.b_o = np.zeros(d_model)

    def split_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, seq_len, d_model) -> (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)"""
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k)
        return x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)

    def merge_heads(self, x):
        """(batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k) -> (batch, seq_len, d_model)"""
        batch, _, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        x = x.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        return x.reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)

    def forward(self, x, mask=None, return_attention=False):
        """Forward pass of multi-head attention.

        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            mask: Optional causal mask
            return_attention: If True, also return attention weights per head

        Returns:
            output: Shape (batch, seq_len, d_model)
            attn_weights: Shape (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len) if requested
        """
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape

        # Step 1: Linear projections
        Q = x @ self.W_q + self.b_q  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        K = x @ self.W_k + self.b_k
        V = x @ self.W_v + self.b_v

        # Step 2: Split into heads
        Q = self.split_heads(Q)  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)
        K = self.split_heads(K)
        V = self.split_heads(V)

        # Step 3: Scaled dot-product attention (all heads in parallel)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0, 1, 3, 2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        # scores shape: (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)

        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)

        attn_weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1)

        # Step 4: Apply attention to values
        context = attn_weights @ V  # (batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_k)

        # Step 5: Merge heads and apply output projection
        context = self.merge_heads(context)  # (batch, seq_len, d_model)
        output = context @ self.W_o + self.b_o

        if return_attention:
            return output, attn_weights
        return output

def softmax(x, axis=-1):

    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

class MultiHeadAttention:
    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads, seed=42):
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / d_model)
        self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale
        self.W_o = rng.randn(d_model, d_model) * scale

    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        batch, seq_len, _ = x.shape
        Q = (x @ self.W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K = (x @ self.W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V = (x @ self.W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(self.d_k)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
        attn = softmax(scores)
        context = attn @ V
        context = context.transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, self.d_model)
        return context @ self.W_o, attn

    e_x = np.exp(x - x_max)
    return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

def multi_head_attention(x, n_heads, W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o, mask=None):
    batch, seq_len, d_model = x.shape
    d_k = d_model // n_heads

    Q = (x @ W_q).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    K = (x @ W_k).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)
    V = (x @ W_v).reshape(batch, seq_len, n_heads, d_k).transpose(0,2,1,3)

    scores = Q @ K.transpose(0,1,3,2) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores + mask * (-1e9)
    attn = softmax(scores)

    context = (attn @ V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(batch, seq_len, d_model)
    return context @ W_o, attn

        for t in range(seq_len):
            row = attn[0, h, t, :t+1]
            row = row[row > 1e-10]
            head_entropies.append(-np.sum(row * np.log(row)))
    avg_entropy = np.mean(head_entropies)

    print(f"  {n_heads:2d} heads (d_k={d_k:2d}): "
          f"diversity={avg_diversity:.4f}, "
          f"avg_entropy={avg_entropy:.3f}, "
          f"output_norm={np.linalg.norm(output):.2f}")

Βασικα Σημεια

  • Η πολυκεφαλη προσοχη εκτελει πολλους υπολογισμους προσοχης παραλληλα, καθεναν με τις δικες του μαθημενες προβολες που λειτουργουν σε υποχωρο διαστασης d_k = d_model / n_heads.
  • Ο συνολικος αριθμος παραμετρων ειναι ο ιδιος με την προσοχη μοναδικης κεφαλης — ανταλλασσουμε εναν μεγαλο χωρο προσοχης με πολλους μικροτερους εξειδικευμενους.
  • Οι κρισιμες λειτουργιες ειναι το split_heads (αναδιαμορφωση + μεταθεση) και το merge_heads (μεταθεση + αναδιαμορφωση), που διαχωριζουν και επανασυναρμολογουν τη διασταση του μοντελου.
  • Διαφορετικες κεφαλες μαθαινουν να συλλαμβανουν διαφορετικους τυπους σχεσεων (συντακτικες, σημασιολογικες, θεσιακες), καθιστωντας το μοντελο πιο εκφραστικο απο οποιοδηποτε μεμονωμενο μοτιβο προσοχης.
  • Τα συγχρονα LLMs χρησιμοποιουν συνηθως d_k=64 η d_k=128 ανα κεφαλη, με τον συνολικο αριθμο κεφαλων να καθοριζεται απο το d_model / d_k.
